data.summary: The eight‑week plan balances new learning with intensive practice, beginning with the student’s weak units (Differential Equations and Applications of Integration) and revisiting them later. Each week uses the full 6 hours for focused topic study, concrete free‑response tasks, and timed practice, culminating in a mixed‑review week before the exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce Differential Equations basics and begin Integration applications
tasks: Read the textbook sections for 7.1 and 7.2; write a one‑page summary of how to set up a differential equation from a word problem.
Do 5 free‑response questions on modeling with differential equations; check answers with the scoring guide.
Watch a video on average value of a function (8.1); solve 4 practice problems.
Complete 6 problems on using integrals to find position from velocity (8.2); verify each solution by differentiating.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of slope fields and continue integration applications
tasks: Sketch slope fields for 3 given differential equations (7.3); label equilibrium solutions.
Complete 4 FRQ style questions requiring reasoning with slope fields (7.4).
Read 8.3 section; solve 5 applied‑context accumulation problems.
Practice finding area between curves (8.4) with 6 varied pairs of functions.

weeks.focus: Live class reinforcement of Differential Equations and start Limits
tasks: Attend live class 11100; take detailed notes on 7.1 and 7.2 examples.
After class, redo the class’s practice problems without notes.
Read sections 1.1 and 1.2; create a cheat‑sheet of limit definitions and notation.
Do 8 limit‑evaluation problems (including tables and graphs) and check with answer key.

weeks.focus: Complete Limits unit and begin Differentiation fundamentals
tasks: Estimate limits from graphs (1.3) with 6 different graphs; write a brief justification for each.
Estimate limits from tables (1.4); complete 5 table‑based problems.
Determine limits using algebraic properties (1.5); solve 7 mixed‑type problems.
Read 2.1 and 2.2; practice computing average and instantaneous rates for 4 functions.
Complete 6 derivative‑notation problems from 2.2.

weeks.focus: Finish Differentiation basics and start Composite/Implicit differentiation
tasks: Estimate derivatives at a point (2.3) with 5 calculator‑free problems.
Connect differentiability and continuity (2.4); prove the relationship for 3 given functions.
Apply the Power Rule (2.5) to 8 polynomial and rational functions.
Learn the Chain Rule (3.1); solve 6 layered‑function derivative problems.
Practice Implicit Differentiation (3.2) with 5 equations; verify results by solving for dy/dx.

weeks.focus: Contextual applications of differentiation and review weak units
tasks: Interpret derivative meaning in context (4.1); write explanations for 3 real‑world scenarios.
Solve straight‑line motion problems (4.2) involving position, velocity, acceleration; 5 complete FRQs.
Work rates and related rates (4.3, 4.4); complete 4 related‑rates problems.
Re‑solve 3 differential‑equation modeling problems from week 1 to reinforce 7.1‑7.2.
Timed 20‑minute mini‑quiz covering weeks 1‑4 material.

weeks.focus: Analytical applications of differentiation and integration review
tasks: Use the Mean Value Theorem (5.1) on 4 functions; write the theorem’s statement each time.
Identify critical points and apply the First Derivative Test (5.2‑5.4) on 6 functions.
Determine intervals of increase/decrease (5.3) for 5 additional functions.
Re‑do 3 average‑value (8.1) and position‑from‑velocity (8.2) problems from week 1 for fluency.
Full‑length timed practice: 2 FRQs from Unit 5 and 2 from Unit 8 (30 min).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed full‑exam practice
tasks: Take a 90‑minute full‑length practice exam under timed conditions.
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide; note any recurring errors.
Do a rapid‑review worksheet covering one key concept from each unit (15 min per unit).
Finish with 5 mixed FRQs chosen from the weakest units (7 and 8) for final confidence boost.

data.final_week_advice: After the mixed‑review week, spend any remaining days doing timed sections, focusing on speed and accuracy. Review your error log, clarify any lingering misconceptions, and get plenty of rest before the exam day.
